access.pack: The owning vehicle is resolved before streaming; an ungranted digest is an empty 404 indistinguishable from an unknown digest.

sync_routes.listed_by: hub-sync-v1@1.3.0, its status-tables.json (hub-sync-v1@1.4.0 publishes no status table, and its OpenAPI lists no 404 on changes-since or on the manifest)

routes.note: no_full_snapshot is the answer for a well-formed vehicle the Hub serves that has no published full snapshot yet, so an empty 404 on the manifest means a malformed vehicle id or that no full snapshot is published yet.
For a well-formed unknown vehicle the Hub answers the JSON envelope where hub-sync-v1@1.3.0 lists an empty 404; this profile changes neither, and an ungranted vehicle is answered as an unknown one.

sync_routes.rule: Each sync route keeps the 404 the Hub gives an unknown vehicle today, and an ungranted vehicle is answered exactly as an unknown vehicle. The manifest and no-op 404s are asserted by this profile, not inherited: hub-sync-v1@1.3.0 lists no 404 for them. The other routes keep what they have.

access.text: Every vehicle-scoped route checks the paired device's vehicle grant. An ungranted vehicle is answered exactly as an unknown vehicle on the same route: 404 vehicle_not_found on JSON routes and an empty-body 404 on /current. Each sync route keeps the 404 the Hub gives an unknown vehicle today, and an ungranted vehicle gets that same 404. hub-sync-v1@1.3.0 lists the JSON vehicle_not_found 404 on changes-since and an empty 404 on signing-keys and prepared-artefacts. It lists no 404 on manifest and no-op, where the Hub answers JSON vehicle_not_found for a well-formed unknown vehicle id and an empty 404 for a malformed one (the manifest also answers an empty 404 for a known vehicle that has no published full snapshot yet); this profile records those two as asserted, not inherited, statuses. GET /v1/vehicles lists only granted vehicles. Packs resolve their owning vehicle before streaming; an ungranted digest is an empty 404 indistinguishable from an unknown digest.

additive_policy: Clients ignore unknown object fields and unknown capability tokens. Servers may add optional fields and tokens within 1.x. Removing or retyping a field, changing an enum value, or changing a route's status set is a new major profile.

capability_advertisement.attributions: Discovery carries attributions when query.enrichment is advertised.
capability_advertisement.home_assistant: Discovery keeps api_versions ["1.0"], protocol "teslatlas-sync", protocol_major 1 and the query.vehicles and query.current tokens.
capability_advertisement.rule: A token is advertised only when its routes are served.

companion_routes.availability: Served by every Hub of this profile whether or not sync.packs is advertised: its 401 and 404 answers do not depend on that token.
companion_routes.note: Only the statuses this profile asserts are listed. hub-sync-v1@1.3.0 also defines 200 and 406 and lists no 404 for this route: the 404 (JSON vehicle_not_found for a well-formed unknown or ungranted vehicle id, an empty body for a malformed one, or an empty body for a known vehicle that has no published full snapshot yet) is asserted by this profile, not inherited from hub-sync-v1. The Hub also answers an empty 400 (an invalid x-teslatlas-sync-capability or x-teslatlas-supported-schemas header) and 503s (empty, or the JSON service_unavailable envelope when the vehicle check fails) on it, which hub-sync-v1@1.3.0 does not list and this profile does not assert.

Only the statuses this profile asserts are listed. hub-sync-v1@1.3.0 lists 200, 206, 401 and an empty 404 for this route; the Hub also answers 406 (schema publication unavailable), 416 (an unsatisfiable Range) and empty 503s (no cursor key, no free stream slot, catalogue errors) on it, which hub-sync-v1@1.3.0 does not list and this profile does not assert.
companion_routes.object_name: The lowercase hex SHA-256 pack digest followed by .sqlite.zst; a name of any other form is an empty 404.

cursor.handling: Preserve byte-for-byte, percent-encode once as query value, never parse or log; limit may change. Reuse against another Hub, vehicle, scope or window fails with 400 invalid_cursor.

legacy.payload_layout: version 1 (1 byte), vehicle UUID (16), from_ms (8), to_ms (8), last start_date_ms (8), last drive id (8)

layout.encoding: signed big-endian; the drive or charge id for nested pages, otherwise 0
signed big-endian; first ordering key of the last emitted item
signed big-endian; id of the last emitted item

cursor.rejected_when: The tag, kind, vehicle, scope id or window differs, or a last key falls outside the window.

tag.domain_prefix: teslatlas-hub/public-query-cursor/v1 followed by one NUL byte
tag.example_key_use: Example cursors only; no Hub uses this key.
tag.message: domain prefix followed by the payload

integers.javascript: decode losslessly or reject values outside [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991] before normalization; never silently round IDs

browser_origin_response.applies_to: every route, including the hub-sync-v1 routes
browser_origin_response.rule: A request that carries an Origin header is answered 403 with an empty body and Cache-Control: no-store, before the route runs, when the Hub does not admit that origin (neither the Hub's own origin nor one of the owner's allowed origins) or the route has no browser access. Which routes admit browser origins, and how the Hub answers a CORS preflight (an OPTIONS request), are set by the Hub and lie outside this profile. A client that sends no Origin header, such as a native client or a conformance run, never sees any of them.

handler_timeout_response.applies_to: every route, including the hub-sync-v1 routes
handler_timeout_response.budget: The 15 second handler budget includes the time spent waiting for one of the 32 in-flight request slots.
handler_timeout_response.rule: When the budget expires the Hub answers 503 with an empty body and no content type, whatever the route. A route that lists a JSON 503 form (service_unavailable, not_ready) still answers an empty body in this case, so a client treats an empty 503 on any route except the claim as a transient outage and may retry. A claim is never retried automatically: the invitation is single use, and a claim that ended in an empty 503 may already have consumed it.

pages.conditional: If-None-Match matching the current ETag returns 304 with an empty body, the same ETag and Cache-Control: no-store.
pages.etag: strong; quoted lowercase hex SHA-256 of the response body
pages.item_split: A page is never split inside an item: it stops before the item that would exceed the byte cap and carries a cursor after the last included item. An item that alone exceeds the cap is 503 service_unavailable.

malformed_query_values.rule: A query value that does not parse as a decimal integer in the parameter's range (limit 0 to 4294967295, from_ms and to_ms signed 64-bit) is 400 invalid_query, for example limit=abc, limit=-1, from_ms=1.5 or to_ms=9223372036854775808. invalid_limit and invalid_time_range apply only to well-formed values: limit=0 or above the route maximum is invalid_limit, and from_ms=-1 or from_ms not below to_ms is invalid_time_range.

query.limit: integer between 1 and the route maximum; default per route
query.to_ms: exclusive; integer >= 0; default 9223372036854775807 (omit the parameter for the default; JavaScript clients never send that value)

response.next_cursor: string, or null on the last page

pages.time_window: from_ms inclusive, to_ms exclusive; default 0 through signed64 maximum; from_ms must be less than to_ms

refused.rule: A name that breaks the rule is answered 422 with a bounded text/plain body before the invitation is consulted: the refusal consumes nothing and does not reveal whether the invitation exists, so the same invitation still claims with a valid name. The name never causes a 503 (an empty 503 for another reason, such as the handler time budget, can still happen, and the claim's never-retry rule then applies).

device_name.rule: device_name is 1 to 128 UTF-8 bytes and has no control character (U+0000 to U+001F, U+007F to U+009F). The schema states the character limit (maxLength 128) and the control-character rule, but a character count cannot state the byte limit: a name of at most 128 characters can still be over 128 bytes, and is refused all the same.

pairing.invitation_lifetime: expiresAtMs epoch milliseconds; default invitation lifetime 900 seconds, owner-configurable; single use.

lifetime.text: Bearer expires_at_ms slides to at most now + 30 days on use and never beyond the device's absolute maximum (owner-configurable, default 180 days from pairing). When rotation cannot move the expiry later, rotate returns 200 with the current bearer and expiry unchanged and reason "max_lifetime", and issues nothing; clients should ask the owner to re-pair before expires_at_ms.

pairing.revocation: POST /v1/device/revoke with the current or grace bearer and no request body revokes the calling device and returns 204 with an empty body. Afterwards the bearer is 401 on every route, so a repeated call returns 401 and clients treat 401 on revoke as already revoked. A request with a non-empty body, including one over 4096 bytes, is 400 and revokes nothing; it is never 413. When paired-device authentication is off, auth.revoke is not advertised and the route answers 404 with an empty body.

rotation.lost_response_retry: A retry of rotate with the prior bearer during the grace window returns the same successor; it never issues a different token.
rotation.old_bearer_validity: The prior bearer stays valid for normal requests through rotation_at_ms + 86400000 exclusive. A retry of rotate with the prior bearer during the grace window returns the same successor; it never issues a different token. After the window the prior bearer is 401.
rotation.one_grace_per_device: Only the bearer replaced by the latest rotation has a grace window; a further rotation ends the earlier bearer's grace, and it is then 401.
rotation.response_fields: device_id, access_token, expires_at_ms and, only at the absolute maximum, reason

pairing.trust: endpoint plus tlsPin (SHA256 of DER leaf certificate); validate TLS identity before sending secret. Fixture uses a private CA trust file and verifies hostname. pairingUri duplicates secret; keep whole invitation private.

path_identifiers.invalid: 404 with the route's not-found JSON (drive_not_found or charge_not_found), never 400, so path probing returns one shape

nil_vehicle_id.rule: The nil UUID is a well-formed vehicle_id that no vehicle can have: it is an unknown vehicle and is answered as any other unknown vehicle, and its value never causes a 503 (a 503 for another reason, such as the handler time budget, can happen to it as to any request).

path_identifiers.spellings: Only the lowercase hyphenated form of a vehicle_id and the plain decimal form of a drive_id or charge_id are specified. A Hub's parser may also accept other spellings of the same value (a UUID in upper case, without hyphens, in braces or as urn:uuid:; an integer with a plus sign or leading zeros) and serve the same resource: a client sends only the specified forms and does not rely on the others being refused.

answers.json_routes: 404 JSON vehicle_not_found for a malformed vehicle_id, drive_not_found or charge_not_found for a malformed drive_id or charge_id
answers.other_sync_routes: changes-since, signing-keys and prepared-artefacts answer as access.sync_routes.routes[].malformed_vehicle_id says

undecodable.rule: A path segment (vehicle_id, drive_id, charge_id or the pack object_name) whose percent-decoding is not valid UTF-8, for example %FF, is a malformed identifier like any other. It is answered after the bearer check, with the malformed-identifier answer of the route below, never 400 and never a framework text/plain body; a request without a valid bearer is 401 whatever its path segments.

routes.in_progress: Only drives that have ended are listed; a drive in progress is left out.

request_fields.device_name: See pairing.device_name: a name the Hub refuses is 422 and consumes nothing.

routes.request_limit: A request body of a JSON media type (application/json or application/*+json) over 4096 bytes is answered 413 with a bounded text/plain body; the request is refused before the claim is attempted. A request whose Content-Type is missing or is not a JSON media type (application/json or application/*+json) is 415 whatever its size.
routes.retry: Never retry a claim automatically after an empty 503, a timeout or a lost response: the invitation is single use and the claim may already have consumed it. A 400, 413, 415 or 422 answer means the claim was not attempted, so the same invitation can be used for a corrected request.

routes.in_progress: A drive in progress is not served: its id is 404 drive_not_found.
The positions of a drive in progress are not served: its id is 404 drive_not_found.
Only closed charge sessions (end_date_ms set) are listed; a charge in progress is left out.
A charge in progress is not served: its id is 404 charge_not_found.
The samples of a charge in progress are not served: its id is 404 charge_not_found.

routes.availability: Clients call it only when discovery advertises auth.revoke. When paired-device authentication is off, auth.revoke is not advertised and the route answers 404 with an empty body, as rotate does.
routes.request_body: none; any non-empty request body, including one over 4096 bytes, is 400, revokes nothing, and the 400 body is not constrained
routes.request_body_limit: The 4096 byte ordinary request-body limit never turns an over-limit body into 413 on this route: a Hub answers 400 for every non-empty body, so it does not read the body through an extractor that answers 413.

sessions.in_progress: A drive or charge in progress is never listed, and its id is 404 drive_not_found or charge_not_found on the item and nested routes.
sessions.served: Closed sessions only: a drive or charge that has an end_date_ms. The drive and charge schemas require it to be non-null.

unauthorized.applies_to: every route with bearer true, including revoke
unauthorized.path_segments: The bearer is checked before the path segments are interpreted: a request without a valid bearer is 401 whatever its vehicle_id, drive_id, charge_id or object_name, including a segment that percent-decodes to invalid UTF-8.

unsupported.revisions: no public current or drive snapshot revision
unsupported.rich_protocol_versions: the root teslatlas-v1 family is not served
unsupported.sse: no public event stream or epoch
